body: U+0023# Post-restart acceptance: the two gates fire, liveU+000AU+000ARestart confirmed the new configuration is in force: six rule files load, the twelve removed ones are reported absent, `machinist` is in the roster and the nine deleted types are gone.U+000AU+000AU+002A*8.10 hold-loop gate: PASS, both directions.**U+000AU+000APositive: running `i=0; until [ $i -ge 3 ]; do sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done` was denied, and the reason returned was my hook's text verbatim - "Hold loops are denied. A subagent result is delivered to you automatically when it completes..." That wording identifies it as this gate rather than the harness's own foreground-sleep block, which was the confound worth ruling out.U+000AU+000ANegative: `for f in alpha beta gamma; do echo "iteration $f"; done` ran normally. A loop without sleep is not a hold loop, and the gate correctly lets it through.U+000AU+000AU+002A*8.11 task-output gate: PASS, both directions.**U+000AU+000APositive: reading a file at `.../tasks/acceptance811.output` was denied with my hook's verbatim reason.U+000AU+000ANegative: reading `.../tasks/acceptance811-control.txt` - same directory, different extension - returned the file normally.U+000AU+000ABoth gates were proven at script level last session over 12 cases including 5 negatives. What was unproven then was harness registration, and that is what these four live calls establish.U+000AU+000AU+002A*8.12 partial, structural half confirmed.** Beyond the depth limit of 1 now set in `env`, none of the five retained agents carries the `Agent` tool in its allowlist - checked by exact-token match on each `tools:` line, not substring. Nesting is therefore blocked two independent ways: the limit, and the absence of the tool that would do it. A live probe of the limit itself is still running.U+000A
